question: When the sandbox dies mid-review, or a round follows earlier Kody suggestions on the same PR, does what reaches the PR match what a correct review delivers — nothing unread, revisions linked, nothing already sent posted again?

cases.checks: Kody Rule (outbound timeout shorter than the function limit) on a file new in the PR; more than 40 later comments push the earlier one out of the history; the fetch line was re-touched and still sets no timeout; stored not_implemented

Kody Rule (test helpers build the concrete error class); the earlier comment covered two helpers, one was fixed and the other only had its line re-touched; stored partially_implemented; more than 40 later comments push it out of the history

Kody Rule (no double casts without a justification) on a file new in the PR; stored implemented, but the as-unknown-as cast is still there with no comment; more than 40 later comments push the earlier one out of the history
Kody Rule (no magic literals for units and quantities) on a Go file new in the PR; stored not_implemented; more than 40 later comments push the earlier one out of the history

Ping-pong on one function: an early comment asked to forward the raw input, a later Kody Rule comment asked to forward only the validated data (stored implemented); the developer forwards the raw object again; 40 earlier comments

delivered.text: The outbound fetch has no timeout, violating rule 21, so if the TZ API stalls it can hang until the platform kills the function at `FUNCTION_LIMIT_SECONDS = 10`, leaving the caller with an unhandled timeout instead of the intended 502. Declare a named constant next to `FUNCTION_LIMIT_SECONDS`, such as `const TZ_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` (it must stay below the 10s function limit), and pass `{ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(TZ_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS) }` as the fetch options so the call fails fast and is handled by the existing `!res.ok` path / error handling.

Pass an explicit `AbortSignal.timeout` signal shorter than the function limit, e.g. define `TZ_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS` as `8_000` next to `FUNCTION_LIMIT_SECONDS` and use it here.

Define a zod schema next to the interface, e.g. `const invoicePaidEventSchema = z.object({ type: z.literal('invoice.paid'), invoiceId: z.string(), amountCents: z.number().int() })`, and replace the cast with `const event = invoicePaidEventSchema.parse(req.body);`, or add a comment justifying the type if the shape is genuinely guaranteed.
